title: Production Evals For Agentic AI Systems - Nishant Gupta, Meta Superintelligence Labs

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling

summary: In this presentation, Nishant Gupta from Meta Superintelligence Labs explores the fundamental shift in evaluating agentic AI systems, moving from traditional offline benchmarks to continuous production evaluation. Gupta argues that benchmarks measure model capability, while production measures system behavior. Agentic systems introduce complex failure modes beyond hallucinations—including memory, retrieval, planning, tool execution, and multi-agent coordination failures. Consequently, evaluation must shift from assessing individual outputs to evaluating entire workflows. Gupta advocates adopting an SRE mindset where reliability, availability, latency, and recovery are prioritized over raw accuracy. He introduces an evaluation pyramid: benchmarks form the base (scalable but limited), scenario-based simulations occupy the middle, and production telemetry sits at the top, providing the highest value signals from real user interactions. Offline evaluations must become scenario-driven, measuring task completion and tool correctness within simulated environments. Once deployed, every production interaction becomes evaluation data. Humans are reframed not as fallback systems, but as crucial evaluators calibrating automated pipelines. Gupta emphasizes that observability and evaluation are inseparable; agent traces must function like distributed tracing in microservices, capturing reasoning paths and tool calls to detect silent drift. He introduces a continuous evaluation loop operating post-deployment, mapping metrics like task completion, escalation rate, and recovery directly to business outcomes. Finally, Gupta outlines a control plane architecture where evaluation continuously observes, collects telemetry, and governs the execution plane, cementing evaluation as a core operational infrastructure rather than a mere testing phase.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

takeaways: Agentic evaluation must shift from measuring model outputs to assessing overall system behavior and workflow execution.
Offline benchmarks are insufficient as they fail to capture tool failures, API outages, and long-running workflow complexities.
Reliability should be the North Star metric for AI systems, treating accuracy as just one input rather than the ultimate goal.
Production telemetry provides the most valuable evaluation signals, transforming real user interactions into evaluation data.
Agent systems require observability via detailed execution traces, similar to distributed tracing in microservices.
Evaluation is an always-running service embedded in the control plane, not a discrete pre-deployment testing phase.
Scenario-based offline evaluations are more effective than prompt-driven tests for simulating realistic agentic workflows.
Humans should act as evaluators providing critical calibration signals, not just as fallback systems for failures.

sections.title: Introduction to Agentic Evaluation
sections.summary: Nishant Gupta introduces the shift from model benchmarking to system behavior evaluation. Benchmarks fail to capture real-world complexities like tool failures and long-running workflows.

sections.title: Hierarchy of Failure Modes
sections.summary: Agentic systems introduce multi-layered failures beyond hallucinations, including memory, safety, reasoning, and multi-agent coordination issues, requiring an SRE mindset focused on reliability.

sections.title: Evaluation Pyramid and Offline Evals
sections.summary: Proposes an evaluation pyramid from benchmarks to production telemetry. Offline evaluations should be scenario-driven, measuring task completion and tool correctness.

sections.title: Production Telemetry and Human Evaluators
sections.summary: Production traffic is the most valuable evaluation data. Humans should be treated as evaluators calibrating automated pipelines, not merely fallback systems.

sections.title: Observability and Continuous Evaluation
sections.summary: Details the need for distributed tracing of agent workflows to detect drift. Evaluation must become an always-running service integrated post-deployment.

sections.title: Metrics, Architecture, and Key Lessons
sections.summary: Maps evaluation metrics to business outcomes and outlines a control plane architecture where evaluation governs the execution plane, concluding with the necessity of treating evaluation as infrastructure.
